title: Universal polynomial norm sections and their open generation locus
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a smooth projective geometrically integral finite-type $F$-scheme of dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-kun-projective, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a finite group acting on $C$ by $F$-automorphisms. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Using module pullback and tensor product [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], put $B=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*L$ and, for $a\in\Gamma(C,L^{\otimes n})$, $\mathcal N_G(a)=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*a\in\Gamma(C,B^{\otimes n})$, with the tensor-power comparison of [def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm]. Fix an integer $n\geq1$ and put $M=B^{\otimes n}$, $V=\Gamma(C,L^{\otimes n})$ and $J=\Gamma(C,M)$. Both vector spaces are finite-dimensional, and for every extension field $E/F$ the canonical scalar-extension maps $V\otimes_FE\to\Gamma(C_E,L_E^{\otimes n})$ and $J\otimes_FE\to\Gamma(C_E,M_E)$ are isomorphisms [def-pc-base-change]. Choose any basis of $V$ and regard $P=V\times V$ as an affine $F$-space. There are universal sections $s_P,t_P$ of the pullback of $M$ to $C\times_FP$ whose specialization at each $v=(a,b)\in P(E)$ is $(\mathcal N_G(a),\mathcal N_G(b))$ for the base-changed action. Their coordinates in any basis of $J$ are homogeneous polynomials of degree $|G|$ in the respective section coordinates. If $p:C\times_FP\to P$ is the projection and $Z\subseteq C\times_FP$ is their common zero scheme (locally cut out by their two coefficients), then $p(|Z|)$ is closed and $U=P\setminus p(|Z|)$ is open. For every extension field $E/F$ and every $v\in P(E)$, one has $v\in U(E)$ if and only if the specialized pair generates $M_E$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. This equivalence also applies when the image of $v$ is a nonclosed point of $P$. For each $k\in G$, the canonical permutation $g\mapsto gk$ of tensor factors identifies $k^*B_E^{\otimes n}$ with $B_E^{\otimes n}$ and carries both pulled-back specialized norm sections to their original sections. Consequently the morphism to $\mathbf P^1_E$ attached to any generating specialized pair is $G$-invariant [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections]. Here the canonical specialized coordinate sections and orbit-bundle base-change identifications are those of [def-sfb-norm-pencil-base-change-sections]; the canonical scalar-extension map is that of [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison] in degree zero. Pullback tensor and power comparisons are those of [def-sc-tensor-pullback-power-comparison], powers of their isomorphisms are those of [def-sfb-tensor-power-pullback-comparisons], and a local frame means a free generator as in [def-sc-local-free-generator].

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, degree zero, and Tag 02O5, lemma-proper-pushforward-coherent. Proper closed image is morphisms.tex Tag 01W0. The equivariant reindexing of the same universal norm pair also carries returned step 17; constructions.tex Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space.

proof.text: Pullback preserves invertibility, and the tensor product of two invertible modules is invertible. Apply these statements to each $g^*L$ and induct over the finite ordered tensor product and the $n$ tensor factors. Thus $L^{\otimes n}$, $B$, $M$ and their pullbacks to $C\times_FP$ and $C_E$ are invertible. Locally each is $\mathcal O$ with one basis vector, so it is quasi-coherent and finitely presented: the local presentation has one generator and no relations.

The structure morphism of $C$ is proper because it is projective. Apply proper coherent finiteness in degree $0$ to the two quasi-coherent finitely presented modules $L^{\otimes n}$ and $M$ from step 1. Degree-zero cohomology is global sections, so $V$ and $J$ are finite-dimensional $F$-vector spaces.

source.place: Tag 02O5, proposition-proper-pushforward-coherent, degree zero; properness from morphisms.tex Tag 01WC, lemma-locally-projective-proper.

proof.text: For every extension field $E/F$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is flat. The scheme $C$ is quasi-compact (its structure morphism is of finite type over the affine $\operatorname{Spec}F$) and separated over $F$ (proper by step 2). Hence the specific comparison $\beta^0:E\otimes_F\Gamma(C,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(C_E,\mathcal F_E)$, $c\otimes x\mapsto c\cdot p^*x$, is bijective for each of $\mathcal F=L^{\otimes n}$ and $\mathcal F=M$; degree-zero cohomology is global sections. These are the two asserted canonical scalar-extension isomorphisms (the proper-scheme flat base change lemma gives the same dimension count). The tensor definition of pullback identifies the pullback of $L^{\otimes n}$ with $L_E^{\otimes n}$: locally both send $a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n$ to $(1\otimes a_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes(1\otimes a_n)$. The same observation identifies pullbacks of $B$ and $M$ with their base-changed orbit-bundle expressions. Explicitly, if $q_E:C_E\to C$ is the projection, base change of each $g$ gives $q_E\circ g_E=g\circ q_E$. The pullback composition isomorphisms therefore identify $g_E^*q_E^*L$ with $q_E^*g^*L$, and on sections both maps send $g^*s$ to its normalized pullback $1\otimes g^*s$.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, (2), i=0; tensor-pullback formula in modules.tex Tag 01CD.

proof.text:
Choose an $F$-basis $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ of $V$, and write $P=\operatorname{Spec}F[x_i,y_i\mid i\in I]$, with $q:C\times_FP\to C$. For every function $\alpha:G\to I$, let $w_\alpha\in J$ be the image of $\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*e_{\alpha(g)}$ under the comparison defining the norm. Define actual global sections by the finite sums
$$s_P=\sum_{\alpha:G\to I}\left(\prod_{g\in G}x_{\alpha(g)}\right)q^*w_\alpha,\qquad t_P=\sum_{\alpha:G\to I}\left(\prod_{g\in G}y_{\alpha(g)}\right)q^*w_\alpha.$$
The coefficients are functions pulled back from $P$. In any basis $(j_r)$ of $J$, write $w_\alpha=\sum_r c_{r,\alpha}j_r$. The displayed coefficients of $q^*j_r$ are then $\sum_\alpha c_{r,\alpha}\prod_g x_{\alpha(g)}$ and its $y$ analogue, homogeneous of degree $|G|$. This is just finite distributivity of the tensor product; no norm-linearity assertion is used.

source.place: Tag 01CA, section-tensor-product; agent finite multilinear expansion of the norm defined by def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm.

proof.text: For $v=(a,b)\in P(E)$, step 3 writes $a=\sum_i a_i(e_i)_E$ and $b=\sum_i b_i(e_i)_E$. Each $g_E$ is over $E$, hence $g_E^*a=\sum_i a_i g_E^*(e_i)_E$. Distributing the tensor product over all $g$ yields $\mathcal N_G(a)=\sum_\alpha(\prod_g a_{\alpha(g)})(w_\alpha)_E$, exactly the restriction of $s_P$ along $1_C\times v$. The identical formula with $b_i$ gives $t_P|_v=\mathcal N_G(b)$. Pullback and the comparison commute here because each sends a local pure tensor to the same tensor with coefficients mapped to $E$. Thus these sections have the asserted specialization for arbitrary $E/F$.

source.place: Tags 01CA and 01CD; agent specialization of the finite expansion in step 4, using the normalized section pullback 1 tensor s.

proof.text: Put $X=C\times_FP$. Form $Z=Z(s_P)\times_X Z(t_P)$ from the two zero schemes of the invertible module $q^*M$. Their local form and the ideal formula for base change of a closed subscheme show that, on a trivializing affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ where $s_P=f e$ and $t_P=h e$, this fibre product is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/(f,h))$. In particular it is a closed subscheme of $X$. The same base-change ideal formula, which holds for arbitrary morphisms, shows that $Z_v=Z\times_P\operatorname{Spec}E$ is cut out by the images of $f,h$ on the pulled-back affine charts. By step 5 it is precisely the common zero scheme of $\mathcal N_G(a),\mathcal N_G(b)$ on $C_E$. No flatness of $v$ is required.

source.place: Tag 01JU, lemma-fibre-product-immersion (1), closed-immersion base change and image ideal; zero-scheme definition from def-pc-zero-scheme.

proof.text: Properness of $C\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ from step 2 includes universal closedness. Its base change $p:C\times_FP\to P$ is therefore a closed map by the definition of universal closedness. Since $|Z|$ is closed in $C\times_FP$ by step 6, $p(|Z|)$ is closed in $P$, and its complement $U$ is open.

source.place: Tag 01W1, definition-proper, and the definition of universal closedness; Tag 01W0 is the containing section, not the lemma.

proof.text: Let $v:\operatorname{Spec}E\to P$ have image $u$. If $Z_v$ has a point, its image is a point of $Z$ over $u$, so $u\in p(|Z|)$. Conversely, if $z\in Z$ maps to $u$, then $\kappa(z)$ and $E$ are extensions of $\kappa(u)$. The common-extension-field lemma gives a field $\Omega$ containing both over $\kappa(u)$. The resulting maps $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z$ through $z$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ agree over $P$, hence define a point of $Z_v$. The map $v$ factors through the open subscheme $U$ exactly when its unique image point $u$ belongs to $U$. Thus $v\in U(E)$ if and only if $Z_v$ is empty. This argument uses the actual residue field $\kappa(u)$ and never assumes that $u$ is closed.

source.place: Tag 0H7K, lemma-common-extension-field, applied over kappa(u); fibre-product universal property.

proof.text: By the generating-sections fibre criterion, the two specialized sections generate $M_E$ exactly when at every point of $C_E$ at least one is nonzero in its one-dimensional residue-field fibre. On a trivializing chart their images are the coefficients $f,h$, so their simultaneous vanishing is exactly the support of the scheme with ideal $(f,h)$ from step 6. Consequently generation is equivalent to $Z_v$ being empty, and step 8 proves the asserted equivalence with $v\in U(E)$.

source.place: Tag 01AM, definition-globally-generated, and Tag 01CY, lemma-s-open, as stated in lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre.

proof.text: Fix $k\in G$ over $E$. Contravariant pullback gives $k^*g^*L_E\simeq(gk)^*L_E$. Tensor these identifications and reindex by the bijection $g\mapsto gk$ to obtain $\lambda_k:k^*B_E\simeq B_E$ and its $n$th tensor power. On $\bigotimes_g k^*g^*a$ this reindexing gives $\bigotimes_g(gk)^*a=\bigotimes_hh^*a$. The norm comparison commutes with this operation: on local pure tensors both orders of operation place the same $n$ tensor factors for each $h$ in the same blocks. More explicitly, numbering the power factors by $j=1,\ldots,n$, both composites send the factor indexed by $(g,j)$ to the factor indexed by $(gk,j)$; the recursive comparison groups these same factors in the prescribed order. Pure tensors locally generate the tensor products, so the maps agree. Hence $\lambda_k^{\otimes n}(k^*\mathcal N_G(a))=\mathcal N_G(a)$, and the same single isomorphism carries $k^*\mathcal N_G(b)$ to $\mathcal N_G(b)$. Only permutation and tensor functoriality enter; faithfulness and division by $|G|$ are unnecessary.

source.place: Tags 01CA and 01CD; agent reindexing calculation for the finite tensor norm with the recursive tensor-power comparison of def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm.

proof.text: For a generating specialized pair let $h:C_E\to\mathbf P^1_E$ be its associated morphism. Compatibility with pullback in the projective-space functor-of-points lemma says that $h\circ k$ corresponds to the pulled-back invertible module and pair. Step 10 gives an isomorphism of this pair with the original one, and equivalent pairs give the same morphism to $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$. Both $h\circ k$ and $h$ have the same structure map to $\operatorname{Spec}E$, since $k$ is an $E$-automorphism. Uniqueness in the fibre-product definition of $\mathbf P^1_E$ therefore gives $h\circ k=h$. This proves $G$-invariance for every such pair.

statement_change.old_statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a smooth projective geometrically integral finite-type $F$-scheme of dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-kun-projective, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a finite group acting on $C$ by $F$-automorphisms. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Using module pullback and tensor product [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], put $B=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*L$ and, for $a\in\Gamma(C,L^{\otimes n})$, $\mathcal N_G(a)=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*a\in\Gamma(C,B^{\otimes n})$, with the tensor-power comparison of [def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm]. Fix an integer $n\geq1$ and put $M=B^{\otimes n}$, $V=\Gamma(C,L^{\otimes n})$ and $J=\Gamma(C,M)$. Both vector spaces are finite-dimensional, and for every extension field $E/F$ the canonical scalar-extension maps $V\otimes_FE\to\Gamma(C_E,L_E^{\otimes n})$ and $J\otimes_FE\to\Gamma(C_E,M_E)$ are isomorphisms [def-pc-base-change]. Choose any basis of $V$ and regard $P=V\times V$ as an affine $F$-space. There are universal sections $s_P,t_P$ of the pullback of $M$ to $C\times_FP$ whose specialization at each $v=(a,b)\in P(E)$ is $(\mathcal N_G(a),\mathcal N_G(b))$ for the base-changed action. Their coordinates in any basis of $J$ are homogeneous polynomials of degree $|G|$ in the respective section coordinates. If $p:C\times_FP\to P$ is the projection and $Z\subseteq C\times_FP$ is their common zero scheme (locally cut out by their two coefficients), then $p(|Z|)$ is closed and $U=P\setminus p(|Z|)$ is open. For every extension field $E/F$ and every $v\in P(E)$, one has $v\in U(E)$ if and only if the specialized pair generates $M_E$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. This equivalence also applies when the image of $v$ is a nonclosed point of $P$. For each $k\in G$, the canonical permutation $g\mapsto gk$ of tensor factors identifies $k^*B_E^{\otimes n}$ with $B_E^{\otimes n}$ and carries both pulled-back specialized norm sections to their original sections. Consequently the morphism to $\mathbf P^1_E$ attached to any generating specialized pair is $G$-invariant [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections].
